question: How many confirmed measles cases will the CDC report in the United States for 2026, as of the update closest to September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Baseline: 3,134 as of the Sept 3 Thursday data cut. CDC states its page reflects cases notified as of noon Thursdays, so the first cut current as of Sept 17 is the Sept 17 cut (published ~Sept 18) — two increments, weighted ~82%, with ~11% on the resolver using the Sept 10 figure at the scheduled Sept 18 00:00Z time and ~7% on a cadence change pushing to a Sept 24 cut. Reference-class anchor (trailing 8-week mean increment ~152 x 2) gives ~3,438; I adjust up because the last three weeks ran +211/+126/+231 and because CDC's federal tally visibly lags state dashboards (PA state 577 vs CDC's Aug-21 PA figure of 371; WI state 94+ vs federal 38), a backlog that mechanically inflates near-term CDC increments even if true transmission plateaus. Adjusting down: Polymarket's ~4.9-5.0k year-end implies ~110/wk averaged over 17 weeks, i.e. traders expect fall deceleration; Amish/Mennonite-community outbreaks historically burn through susceptibles in 3-6 months and PA's started ~June-July; the 2026 weekly series itself has shown +94 weeks immediately after +200 weeks. Net: ~+195/wk over two cuts. Upper escape (>3,900) needs a one-off backlog reconciliation of the several-hundred-case state-federal gap or a third data cut plus acceleration — priced at 3.5%. Lower bound is closed and safe: the count is monotone non-decreasing.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: Resolves off the CDC 'Measles Cases and Outbreaks' page headline cumulative confirmed-2026 count (https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) — NOT state health-department dashboards, NOT rash-onset epi-curve counts, NOT media tallies. Headline count only; the split between US jurisdictions and international visitors is irrelevant. Fine print: if a page update lands on/after Sept 17 but its data-as-of date is earlier, the resolver waits for the first figure current as of Sept 17 or later.

EVENT WINDOW: Cumulative Jan 1 2026 -> the first CDC data cut current as of 2026-09-17, per the criteria. As of Now (2026-09-07T00:20Z), the most recent published cut is data-as-of Sept 3 (page updated Sept 4); 96% of the Jan 1 -> Sept 17 calendar window has elapsed and roughly 0 of the 2 remaining Thursday data cuts have published.

CADENCE / MECHANICS:
- CDC page text states updates 'reflect only confirmed measles cases notified to CDC as of noon on Thursdays'; page typically posts the following day (Sept 3 cut -> page updated Sept 4). (cdc.gov, retrieved 2026-09-07)
- Thursdays remaining before Sept 17: Sept 10 and Sept 17. Sept 17 is itself a Thursday.
- At least one 2026 update was published late: the Aug 27 cut was reported as a 'delayed' posting. (medicaldaily.com, Aug 2026)
- The count is cumulative and monotone non-decreasing; CDC has not published a downward revision of the 2026 headline this year that I found.

OBSERVED CDC WEEKLY INCREMENTS, 2026 (base rate computed over consecutive CDC data cuts in the active-outbreak period Jul-Sep 2026): Jul 23->Jul 30 +53 (2,318->2,371); Jul 30->Aug 7 +94 (->2,465); Aug 7->Aug 14 +101 (->2,566); Aug 14->Aug 21 +211 (->2,777); Aug 21->Aug 27 +126 (->2,903); Aug 27->Sep 3 +231 (->3,134). Sources: CIDRAP weekly write-ups, Jul 30 / Aug 21 / Sep 4 2026. Mean over these six = 136; mean over the last three = 189. Two-week sums over the same period: 147, 195, 312, 337, 357.

BROADER BASE RATES (different conditioning): over all of 2026 Jan 1 -> Sep 3, 3,134 cases in 35 weeks = ~90/week unconditional. Over 2025 full year: 2,289 cases = ~44/week. Conditional on the current Pennsylvania/Ohio/Wisconsin-driven regime (post-Aug 14), the weekly figure is materially different from either unconditional rate — use the conditional series above, not the annual average.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD LARGER INCREMENTS:
- Pennsylvania state dashboard reported ~577 cases as of Sept 4, with +115 in the prior week and +86 the week before; Lancaster County (Amish/Mennonite) is the epicenter. (CIDRAP / NBC News, Sept 4 2026)
- Federal tally lags state dashboards materially: PA state 497 vs CDC's Aug-21 state-level listing of 371; Wisconsin state 94 confirmed + 6 probable vs federal 38. Described as two reporting systems on different clocks, not an error. (medicaldaily.com, early Sept 2026) This backlog enters future CDC cuts by report date regardless of onset timing.
- Wisconsin rose from 26 to 144 cases in roughly one month; Ohio from ~60 to 129 over the same span. (NBC News, Sept 4 2026)
- Kindergarten MMR coverage fell from 95.2% (2019-20) to 92.4% (2025-26), below the 95% herd-immunity threshold; 94% of 2026 cases were unvaccinated or unknown status. (CDC via Xinhua/Zaobao, Sept 5 2026)
- CDC's Dr. Demetre Daskalakis: 'Measles is acting like it's endemic now. There's a lot of domestic transmission,' and said he would expect 5,000-plus cases this year. Dr. Noel Brewer: 'There's no end in sight.' (NBC News, Sept 4 2026)
- 38 new outbreaks in 2026 with 95% of cases outbreak-associated; 47 jurisdictions reporting. Late-August/September school return coincides with the current epicenters.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD SMALLER INCREMENTS:
- The 2026 weekly series is volatile and non-monotone: a +211 week was immediately followed by +126, and the earlier July weeks ran +53 to +101. Single high weeks have not persisted.
- Utah's outbreak, the year's largest state total earlier in 2026 (514 cases), reported zero new cases in one late-July week; South Carolina (670 cases, the year's largest state total) and Arizona were reported as slowing. Texas fell from 803 cases in 2025 to 188 in 2026; Arizona from 222 to 108. (CIDRAP Jul 30 2026; Becker's / Axios 2026)
- Historical analogue: the 2014 Ohio Amish outbreak produced ~383 cases and burned through its susceptible pool over roughly four months. PA's Lancaster cluster is reported as beginning around June-July 2026.
- Full-year prediction-market pricing (Polymarket, $7.9M volume, resolves Jan 1 2027 off the CDC counter; Manifold) implies a year-end total whose average weekly accrual over the remaining ~17 weeks is well below the last three observed weekly increments — i.e. traders are pricing fall deceleration. Note this contract's deadline (Dec 31) and threshold structure do not match this question's Sept-17 snapshot.
- CDC declines to include the two Pennsylvania deaths in its official count for lack of confirmation, indicating conservative federal adjudication of state-reported events generally.

- Any prediction market or bookmaker contract on the CDC count at a mid-September 2026 snapshot date; all located contracts are full-year 2026 totals. - Week-by-week numeric values from the CDC 'weekly measles cases by rash onset date' epi curve — the chart exists on the page but the underlying figures were not retrievable via text extraction, so I could not check whether onset-date incidence is rising, flat, or falling.
- A current CDC state-by-state table dated Sept 3; the page text retrieved listed only the 47 jurisdictions collectively, and the most recent state-level federal figures I could source were dated Aug 21.
- Any CDC announcement of a change to the weekly update cadence, or any scheduled fed
calls.reference_class: CDC weekly 'Measles Cases and Outbreaks' cumulative-count updates during the active 2026 US multi-state outbreak — specifically the two-consecutive-Thursday-data-cut increment applied to the current published total

calls.reasoning: Resolution needs the CDC figure current as of 2026-09-17; data-as-of has been Thursday since Aug 27, so Sep 10 and Sep 17 are the two remaining updates and the base case is 3,134 plus two weekly increments. Trailing increments are +94, +101, +211, +126 (6-day), +231 - mean ~157/wk but visibly accelerating, with Pennsylvania alone contributing 115 of the last 231 (577 state cases as of Sep 3, Lancaster-area Plain communities, school year underway). Offsetting: Utah's outbreak has flattened, South Carolina's was declared over, Arizona is adding ~2/wk, so the non-PA base is thinner than the headline acceleration suggests, and Labor Day (Sep 7) likely depresses the Sep 10 reporting week with catch-up on Sep 17. I center the two-week sum near +390 (~195/wk), between the trailing mean and the last two weeks' pace. Upside tail past 3,900 needs +766 in two weeks (~383/wk, 1.65x the year's largest increment, twice running) - unlikely on its own; the real mechanism is a timing slip (CDC reverting to a Wednesday as-of date, or skipping the Sep 17 update), which would pull in a third increment. I price that slip at ~15% and the combined escape at 6%. No market contract matches these terms; the year-end Polymarket book implies fall decay, which does not bind a two-week horizon.

CADENCE FACT: data-as-of was Friday through 2026-08-21 and Thursday from 2026-08-27 onward (Aug 27 and Sep 3 are both Thursdays); the Sep 3 figure was posted Fri Sep 4. Sep 10, Sep 17 and Sep 24 are all Thursdays. In 2025 the same page ran on a Wednesday as-of / Friday-publication rhythm - i.e. the as-of weekday has moved at least twice across the two years. BASE RATES, WITH THE CLASS EACH IS OVER: (a) over all 5 trailing 2026 updates Jul 31-Sep 3, mean increment ~157/week (SD ~62, range 94-231); (b) over just the 2 most recent updates (Aug 21 and Sep 3, i.e. conditional on the post-Aug-21 regime), ~192/week normalized to 7 days; (c) over the full 2026 year to date, 3,134 cases across 36 weeks = ~87/week, with increments as low as +30 earlier in the year; (d) over the same-length 14-day windows across 2026, increments have spanned roughly +60 to +440 depending on regime. The conditioning variable that matters is which regime the next two weeks belong to.

EVIDENCE - UPWARD DIRECTION: Pennsylvania contributed 115 of the 231 new cases in the week to Sep 3 (state total 577 on the CDC tally; PA DOH separately reported 540 cases across 36 counties and 91 hospitalizations as of Wed Sep 2), CIDRAP 2026-09-04 and local21news 2026-09; PA's outbreak is centered on Lancaster County Plain (Amish/Mennonite) communities whose parochial school year is underway, CIDRAP/Post-Gazette Sep 2026. Ohio had 15 counties affected as of late Aug, up 4 in one week, CIDRAP 2026-08-21. 38 outbreaks reported in 2026 with 95% of cases (2,969/3,134) outbreak-associated, CDC 2026-09-04. Kindergarten MMR coverage fell from 95.2% (2019-20) to 92.4% (2025-26), CDC via Xinhua/Zaobao 2026-09-05. Measles serial interval is ~10-14 days, so transmission seeded before Sep 3 is still in the reporting pipeline. Labor Day (Mon 2026-09-07) travel was flagged by PA DOH as an exposure risk, CIDRAP 2026-09-04.

EVIDENCE - DOWNWARD / DAMPING DIRECTION: Utah's outbreak, the year's largest, added no new cases in the week to Aug 21 and has been reported flat around the 500s, CIDRAP Aug 2026. South Carolina's outbreak was declared over, CIDRAP 2026. Arizona added 2 cases in a recent week (93 for the year), CIDRAP 2026. Ohio's contribution fell to +15 in the week to Sep 3 from +73 two weeks earlier, CIDRAP. The +94 and +101 weeks in early August show the series can sit near half the current pace within the same season. Labor Day falls inside the Sep 4-10 reporting week, shortening state health departments' working week. Two increments of +211 and +231 following two of +94 and +101 raise the possibility that part of the recent jump is reporting catch-up rather than incidence.

CONTAMINANTS TO IGNORE: Pennsylvania has reported 2 measles-associated deaths (Lancaster County coroner attribution) which CDC has NOT added to its own death count, and NCHS holds no 2026 death record with measles as underlying cause - this is a live public dispute but has no bearing on the confirmed-CASE count. Global outbreaks (Bangladesh ~18,578 cases; Indonesia ~10,453 suspected) are unrelated to the US figure. PAHO deferred its decision on US measles elimination status to November 2026 - after this question's horizon.

MARKETS: no contract was found whose threshold, deadline and resolution source match this question. Polymarket runs a 2026 full-year measles market (Dec 31 deadline, tiered thresholds, ~$7.9M volume since launch 2026-06-30) and ran monthly by-end-of-month variants earlier in the year; Kalshi has a 'kxmeasles' series page but it returned HTTP 429 and no prices were retrieved. Manifold and Polymarket title searches by the harness found no candidate.

Left tail is fattened by ~12% weight on a resolver snapshotting at the nominal Sep 18 00:00Z timestamp, which would capture only the Sep 10 figure (~3,320s), since the Sep 17 cut posts Friday Sep 18. calls.reconciliation: The three runs agreed on instrument (CDC page headline count only), baseline (3,134 as of Sep 3), and the two-increment base case; medians spanned only 3,505-3,524. Disputes were (a) how much weight the one-increment/early-snapshot path deserves, (b) whether to center on the trailing-5 mean (157/wk) or the recent regime (~195-199/wk), (c) upper-escape probability (3%/6%/3%), (d) dispersion (340/400/470). No web access on this run, so factual disputes were settled from the dossiers where the dossiers agreed. Settled factually: the CDC as-of weekday has been Thursday since Aug 27 and the Sep 3 cut posted Friday Sep 4 -- all three runs independently report this, so the Sep 17 cut posts Fri Sep 18, AFTER the scheduled 2026-09-18T00:00:00Z timestamp. That publication-vs-timestamp gap is the one mechanically important fact and it justifies non-trivial weight (12%) on a truncated one-increment resolution, which Run 2 essentially ignored. Not settleable: whether the +211/+231 jump is rising incidence or reporting catch-up -- all three runs tried and failed to retrieve the rash-onset epi-curve figures; I let it stay uncertain, noting it points the same direction over a two-week horizon either way. Judgment calls I took rather than split: center on the recent regime (~190/wk) rather than the diluted trailing-5 mean, because the +94/+101 weeks predate the Pennsylvania acceleration; and place the extra dispersion on the LEFT (early-snapshot branch, a named mechanism) rather than the right, which is why my 90th (3,672) sits below all three runs while my 10th (3,315) sits below Runs 1 and 2. Median 3,500 is marginally below the pool not as a hedge but because the 12% truncation branch is a downside mechanism no averaging captures. Reference class carried forward from Run 3's framing (two-week increments of the CDC 2026 series, conditioned on the current regime); I agree with it.
